public_rationale: He inferred the burn from OpenAI raising $10 billion in June and $8.3 billion in August. But raising money is not burning it. OpenAI's shareholder disclosures, reported by The Information and Reuters, show a cash burn of $2.5 billion for all of January to June 2025, with about $17.5 billion in cash at the end of June. In late September, after June to August had passed, OpenAI was reported to be on track for an $8.5 billion cash-burn target for the whole of 2025. A year's burn of about $8.5 billion cannot include a two-month burn of $10 billion or more. Larger accounting figures exist: a first-half net loss of $13.5 billion, more than half of it non-cash, and a full-year operating loss of about $20.9 billion. Even these average well under $10 billion per two months, and they are not cash burn. 'Appears' softens the claim, but its quantity was off by several times.
limitations: No reported figure matches the exact two-month window. The result relies on first-half actuals and a full-year target.
All figures are press reports of private disclosures, not published audited accounts.
Read as accounting net loss with lumpy non-cash charges, a two-month figure near $10 billion cannot be fully ruled out. But that is not 'burn' in its ordinary sense.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: OpenAI appears to have burned at least ten billion dollars in the two months before this August 2025 post.

statement.excerpt: So, as a reminder, OpenAI appears to have burned at least ten billion dollars in the last two months.

our_interpretation: 'Burned' is read as net cash burn (cash going out, net), its ordinary meaning in startup finance. Non-cash accounting charges are not burn.
'The last two months' is read as roughly early June to early August 2025, the two months before the 6 August 2025 post.

'Appears' hedges the claim. Even so, it asserts a specific quantity with a threshold of $10 billion or more. It is tested by whether OpenAI's reported cash burn makes that quantity plausible. Money raised is not money burned.
criteria.support_condition: Reported figures show OpenAI's net cash burn over roughly June to early August 2025 was $10 billion or more, or come close enough that it plausibly appeared so.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reported figures show OpenAI's cash burn in and around that window was far below $10 billion. An example would be a first-half 2025 burn and a full-year target that together make a $10 billion two-month burn impossible or implausible.

evidence.excerpt: OpenAI said it burned $2.5 billion, in large part due to its research and development costs for developing artificial intelligence and for running ChatGPT
evidence.publisher: Reuters (via The Star), citing The Information
evidence.explanation: OpenAI's cash burn for all of January to June 2025 was $2.5 billion, so June alone was at most about $2.5 billion. For two months to reach $10 billion, July and early August would need $7.5 billion or more. The full-year target in e2 rules that out.

evidence.excerpt: OpenAI looks to meet its full-year revenue target of $13 billion and a cash-burn target of $8.5 billion
evidence.publisher: Reuters (via The Star), citing The Information
evidence.explanation: In late September 2025, with the June to August months already known, OpenAI was reported to be on track for $8.5 billion of cash burn for the whole year. That is less than the $10 billion claimed for two months.

evidence.excerpt: OpenAI during the first half of 2025 collected $4.3 billion in revenue while still posting a net loss of $13.5 billion during that six month period.
evidence.locator: paragraph beginning 'According to a report published last month'
evidence.explanation: The accounting net loss was much larger than cash burn. The same article says more than half of it came from remeasuring convertible interests, a non-cash item. Even this six-month loss works out to about $4.5 billion per two months on average. Net loss is not cash burn.

evidence.excerpt: total costs and expenses reached $34 billion, producing an operating loss of $20.92 billion.
evidence.locator: section before 'The key 2025 figures at a glance'
evidence.explanation: OpenAI's full-year 2025 operating loss, from leaked statements, was about $20.9 billion, an average of about $3.5 billion per two months. Even this broader measure does not suggest $10 billion in the June to July window.
